---
title: "Benchmarking Goals and Context"
---

Before diving into benchmarking, consider what you want to learn. Your goals
determine which criterium features and analysis methods are most appropriate.

## What is your goal in benchmarking?

Common benchmarking goals include:

- **Performance validation**: Verify code meets latency requirements
- **Regression detection**: Catch performance degradations
- **Implementation comparison**: Choose between alternative approaches
- **Optimization guidance**: Identify where optimization effort pays off
- **Capacity planning**: Understand throughput limits

## Is this code on a hotpath?

Code executed frequently (hotpaths) receives aggressive JIT optimization.
Infrequently executed code may never be fully optimized.

| Execution Pattern | Warmup Approach | See |
|-------------------|-----------------|-----|
| Hotpath (called millions of times) | Full JIT warmup with varied inputs | [Warmup](./warmup.html) |
| Occasional (called periodically) | Reduced warmup, measure cold performance | [Quickstart](./quickstart.html) |
| One-shot (startup, initialization) | Minimal warmup, focus on first-call time | [Analysis and View Options](./analysis_and_view_options.html) |

## What is the normal calling pattern?

The JIT optimizes based on observed inputs. Warmup should use representative
arguments to avoid over-specialization.

**Questions to consider:**

- What argument sizes occur in production?
- Is there variation in input characteristics?
- Are there multiple calling contexts?

Use `:warmup-args-fn` to provide varied inputs during warmup. See
[Warmup](./warmup.html) for techniques.

## In-place or isolated measurement?

| Approach | Use When | See |
|----------|----------|-----|
| **Isolated** (standalone bench) | Measuring algorithm performance independent of system | [Quickstart](./quickstart.html) |
| **In-place** (instrumented) | Understanding performance in production context | [In-Situ Measurement](./in_situ.html) |
| **Sampled** (periodic capture) | Long-running systems with minimal overhead | [In-Situ Measurement](./in_situ.html) |

## Typical or unusual performance?

| Interest | Analysis Method | See |
|----------|-----------------|-----|
| **Typical** (mean, median) | Standard statistics | [Quickstart](./quickstart.html) |
| **Distribution shape** | KDE, histogram | [Non-Parametric Analysis](./non_parametric_analysis.html) |
| **Worst-case latency** | Tail analysis, percentiles | [Tail Analysis](./tail_analysis.html) |
| **Fitting models** | Distribution fitting | [Parametric Analysis](./parametric_analysis.html) |

## Single point or range of inputs?

| Scope | Approach | See |
|-------|----------|-----|
| **Single input size** | Standard bench | [Quickstart](./quickstart.html) |
| **Range of sizes** | Domain benchmarking | [Domain Complexity Analysis](./domain_complexity_analysis.html) |
| **Complexity analysis** | Domain with model fitting | [Domain Complexity Analysis](./domain_complexity_analysis.html) |
| **Automated sweeps** | Domain builder | [Domain Complexity Analysis](./domain_complexity_analysis.html) |

## Comparing implementations?

| Comparison Type | Approach | See |
|-----------------|----------|-----|
| **Two implementations** | Run bench on each, compare means | [Quickstart](./quickstart.html) |
| **Multiple implementations** | Domain with :impl axis | [Domain Comparison Analysis](./domain_comparison_analysis.html) |
| **Scaling comparison** | Domain analysis across sizes | [Domain Complexity Analysis](./domain_complexity_analysis.html) |

## Additional considerations

### Memory and allocations

If allocation pressure matters, enable allocation tracking using the
`:allocation-analysis` bench plan (see [Analysis and View Options](./analysis_and_view_options.html)).
